title: Longest Palindromic Substring
statement:
You are given a string made up of printable characters. A palindrome is a sequence of characters that reads the same forward and backward (for example, "level" or "a").

Your task is to find a contiguous run of characters (a substring) from the given string that is a palindrome and is as long as possible. If there are multiple substrings that achieve the maximum length, you may return any one of them.

Note that a substring must occupy consecutive positions in the original string, you cannot skip or reorder characters. Every single character on its own counts as a palindrome of length one, so a valid answer always exists.

Think about how to avoid recomputing the same palindrome checks over and over: naive brute force checks every possible substring, but there are smarter approaches using dynamic programming, expanding outward from each possible center, or the linear-time Manacher's algorithm.

examples.explanation: The substring "geeksskeeg" reads the same forward and backward and is the longest such palindromic run in the string; shorter palindromes like "eksske" also exist inside it but are not maximal.
"anana" is a palindrome of length 5 and is the longest one present. Note that "banab" is not a valid answer since it does not appear as a contiguous substring of "banana".

constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters (letters, digits, punctuation, and spaces)
